title: Learn to Keep People Dependent on You
summary: To cultivate and maintain power, you must make others depend on you for their success, security, and well-being. By mastering an irreplaceable skill or holding vital strategic leverage, you ensure that masters cannot afford to replace you. Power relies on mutual dependency where you hold the upper hand, guided by necessity and fear rather than love, while ensuring their need for you is never fully satisfied.
example: Otto von Bismarck made Prussian kings completely dependent on his political mind and governing ability, allowing him to pull the strings of power and unite Germany.
An astrologer saved his own life from King Louis XI by predicting that he would die three days before the king, forcing Louis to keep him safe and well-cared for.
Mercenaries who solved immediate crises were killed or imprisoned once they were no longer needed because they failed to establish long-term dependency.
Henry Kissinger established extensive network dependencies across multiple departments to make himself essential.
reversal: Complete independence or standing entirely alone at the top without depending on anyone.
Total independence brings isolation, extreme stress, constant pressure, and vulnerability.
